clue.text: Sarcastic about American movement that's not voluntary

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
a tic is an involuntary twitch of a muscle

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at an American protest movement that people were forced to join.
explanation.definitionFit: Caustic remarks are biting and scornful, the same sharp tone as sarcastic ones.

clue.text: "Coy mistress" said native of Minnesota once

indicators.note: said tells us the words before it are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: coy means shy, and Anne serves as the name of a mistress, giving shy Anne

explanation.surface: Reads like a remark about Marvell's poem To His Coy Mistress, then swerves to a Native American people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coy mistress' is a woman's description: SHY ANNE, spoken, gives the people's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne people lived in what is now Minnesota before moving west onto the Great Plains.

clue.text: Animals try bid to unsettle other groups of musicians

indicators.note: unsettling the letters of these words throws them out of their order into a new one

explanation.surface: The Animals, a 1960s band, try a bid to rattle rival bands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Animals are a band, so the brass-and-drum outfits of the answer are 'other' groups of musicians; 'to unsettle' rearranges ANIMALS TRY BID.
explanation.definitionFit: Military bands are ensembles of players attached to army regiments, performing at parades and ceremonies.

clue.text: Country musician Kooper I rage about

parts.note: Al Kooper is the musician who played organ on Dylan's Like a Rolling Stone

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country singer fumes at session man Al Kooper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' poses as the music genre beside 'musician' but is the definition; 'about' rearranges I RAGE. Al Kooper played organ for Dylan.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a nation of North Africa, the largest on the continent by area.

clue.text: Lounger rising late securing cushy job at last

indicators.note: securing means holding something within, so one piece sits inside another
in a down entry rising means the word is read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: the late person is a dead one

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A lazy person who gets up late still lands a soft job in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns DEAD into DAED, and 'securing' places the last letters of cushy and job, Y and B, in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A daybed is a couch for resting on in the daytime, a piece of furniture to lounge on.

clue.text: One who shot his bolt taking lines and acid originally is very revealing

indicators.note: taking means the first piece collects the following pieces after it

parts.note: William Tell shot a crossbow bolt at the apple on his son's head

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Someone who has given up, on lines of cocaine and LSD, spills every secret.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'shoot one's bolt' is to be spent, but here it is literal: Tell's crossbow bolt. 'taking' adds A (first of acid) and LL to TELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tell-all book or interview discloses private details without holding anything back.

clue.text: Singer-songwriter, very unwell, finding solace finally in country's capital

parts.note: Graham Nash is a singer-songwriter of Crosby, Stills and Nash
unwell means ill

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it governs

explanation.surface: A sick singer-songwriter seeks comfort in a nation's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' is country music, not a nation: Nashville is its home. Dylan recorded Nashville Skyline there.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville, Tennessee, is the centre of the country music industry, home of the Grand Ole Opry.

clue.text: Girl needing guide through underworld realm of the dead

indicators.note: something running through another is inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Hel is the Norse underworld, the realm of the dead
an A-Z is a British street map guide

explanation.surface: A girl needs someone to lead her through the land of the dead, like Orpheus or Dante.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a British book of street maps. Hazel is also a Dylan song.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel is a female given name, so a girl may be called it.

clue.text: Hopefully this won't get you Knocked Out Loaded before Highway 61 Revisited

definitions.text: Hopefully this won't get you Knocked Out Loaded before Highway 61 Revisited

parts.words: Hopefully this won't get you Knocked Out Loaded before Highway 61 Revisited
parts.note: a last drink before leaving that you hope will not leave you drunk at the wheel; Knocked Out Loaded and Highway 61 Revisited are Dylan albums

explanation.surface: Two Dylan album titles strung into a warning about drinking before driving.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a final drink taken before setting off home, here a parting drink before driving the highway.

clue.text: Broadcaster's policy for Horizon

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's editorial stance for the BBC science series Horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: Horizon is also a BBC science programme, so the clue reads as TV business. Nashville Skyline is a Dylan album.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyline is the outline where land or buildings meet the sky, the visible horizon.

clue.text: Singer Simon sent back Bob's 2016 prize

indicators.note: something sent back goes in the reverse direction, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Simon Le Bon is the singer of Duran Duran

explanation.surface: Simon returns the award Bob Dylan won in 2016.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer Simon' wants Paul Simon, but it is Simon Le Bon.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016 for his songwriting.

clue.text: Compete with new article about city in which Bob offered to pose or play

definitions.text: city in which Bob offered to pose or play

parts.note: to vie is to compete

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word before it is written backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A city where Dylan told photo-snapping fans he could either play or pose.
explanation.walkthrough: At a 2019 Vienna concert Dylan told fans taking photos 'We can either play or we can pose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria, where that concert took place.

clue.text: Heart of Mine: revolutionary's Obviously 5 Believers (actually none)

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, dropping both ends

parts.note: Fidel Castro was the Cuban revolutionary; Fidel's gives FIDELS

explanation.surface: A list of Dylan song titles: Heart of Mine and Obviously 5 Believers.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart of Mine and Obviously 5 Believers are Dylan songs; Infidels is a Dylan album.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidels are unbelievers, so 'believers, actually none' describes people without faith.

clue.text: Reported looks of a chronicler of his age

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the word following is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: peeps are quick looks

explanation.surface: Accounts of how a historian of his era appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: The diarist's name is pronounced 'peeps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept a diary recording London life in the 1660s, including the Great Fire.

clue.text: Follow something on an album (one with blood on?)

definitions.text: something on an album (one with blood on?)
definitions.meaning: a ... is a song on a record; Blood on the ... is a Dylan album

explanation.surface: Trace an item on a record that seems to be bloodstained.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracking a quarry means pursuing it, and a single recorded song on an LP is called a track.

clue.text: Gas about formerly getting openings for Rolling Thunder gigs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the others

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas
once means formerly

indicators.note: openings are the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Talk of the gigs that once opened Dylan's Rolling Thunder Revue tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolling Thunder Revue was Dylan's 1975-76 tour; 'Gas' is not chatter but CS tear gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigs are live performances by musicians, the informal word for concerts.

clue.text: Form I see creating great work

parts.note: a form is a school class
the letter C is pronounced like see

explanation.surface: A pupil reflects that the school year produces a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: A British school class is called a form.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of lasting excellence, the standard example of its kind.

clue.text: Artist upset after music award mostly for use of language

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
mostly means almost all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a Grammy is an American music award

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is upset after a music prize over how words were used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the artist round; 'mostly' cuts the last letter of the award; 'after' places the artist second. RA stands for Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is the system of rules governing how a language is put together and used.

clue.text: Take pains to get money from Russia after start of tour

indicators.note: after puts the money behind the letter
start of points to the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A traveller takes care to get roubles once the trip begins.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'trouble' oneself is to make an effort, as in 'he troubled to write'.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubling to do something means making the effort, the same as taking pains over it.

clue.text: One final song from Captain Cook?

parts.note: a means one
last means final
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A sea shanty sung for the explorer Captain James Cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Not James Cook the explorer but Alastair Cook, who captained England's cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastair Cook captained the England Test cricket side, so the forename identifies that captain.

clue.text: Wild when bible's assimilated by wise man

indicators.note: assimilated by means taken inside the following piece

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A wise man absorbs scripture while living in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage means fierce and untamed, as wild animals are.

clue.text: Depended on lines to express craving (feeling after One Too Many Mornings)

definitions.text: craving (feeling after One Too Many Mornings)

parts.note: hung means depended, as in hung from a hook
RY, railway, means lines of track

explanation.surface: Someone relied on scripted words to voice their longing, the morning after too much.
explanation.walkthrough: One Too Many Mornings is a Dylan song; the parenthesis adds to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hungry means wanting food, an appetite felt after skipping breakfast.

clue.text: Divine being's returned redeemed

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a deva is a Hindu god, so deva's gives DEVAS

explanation.surface: A god comes back and is saved.
explanation.walkthrough: Saved is a Dylan gospel album.
explanation.definitionFit: To be redeemed in the religious sense is to be saved from sin.

clue.text: Piece of music that's short, to a greater extent in audition

indicators.note: in audition means as heard, so the phrase is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: more so means to a greater extent

explanation.surface: A brief tune makes a bigger impression in a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a tryout for musicians but signals the sound of MORE SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A morceau is a short piece of music, from the French for a bit or morsel.

clue.text: Mournful song from first of Dylan's Island records with two chords

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of each of the three words

parts.note: G and E are musical chords

explanation.surface: A sad song from Dylan's early recordings on the Island label, using only two chords.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirge is a song on Dylan's album Planet Waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a lament for the dead, slow and sorrowful.

clue.text: Former quiz show host losing heart with stripped Disney heroine revealing something hairy

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the name drops out

parts.note: Chris Tarrant hosted the British Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters are peeled off the name

parts.note: Mulan is the heroine of the Disney film

explanation.surface: A TV host and a stripped-off Disney heroine reveal something hairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops the middle R of TARRANT; 'stripped' takes M and N off MULAN. Tarantula is Dylan's 1971 book.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large spider with a body covered in hair.
